professional_summary: The last-day screen yielded one especially strong baryon-rich heavy-ion transport comparison, one model-sensitive proposal for dynamical bubble-nucleus signatures, and two adjacent QCD/nuclear-theory results. The most transferable AI/ML lesson is methodological: compositional out-of-distribution predictions should be compared with simple structured baselines and calibrated against held-out truth. No new experimental heavy-ion paper met the inclusion bar in the screened window.
strongest_paper_summary: A controlled PHSD5.2 versus hadron-string comparison identifies a strangeness-ordered response and maps it to experimentally accessible excitation functions and elliptic flow.

papers.title: Strange-quark-number-dependent response to partonic dynamics in baryon-rich Au+Au collisions
papers.short_authors: Di Zhao, Xun Zhu, Gao-Chan Yong
papers.abstract: We identify a strange-quark-number-dependent hierarchy in the response to explicit partonic dynamics by comparing PHSD5.2 with its hadron--string limit in baryon-rich Au+Au collisions at √sNN=3.0–7.2 GeV. The hierarchy is strongest in fractional yields at the upper end of the scan, while abundant-hadron flow changes little at lower energies. The proposed discriminants are matched Ξ−/Λ and Ω−/Λ excitation functions together with high-mT proton elliptic flow.

papers.title: Collective-flow signatures of bubble nuclei in intermediate-energy projectile fragmentation reactions
papers.short_authors: Ge Ren, Chun-Wang Ma, Xi-Guang Cao, Kai-Xuan Cheng, Jie Pu
papers.abstract: The paper studies collective flow in 40Ca+9Be at 140 MeV/u with an extended quantum molecular dynamics model. The projectile is initialized as a relaxed ten-alpha cluster configuration with a bubble-like density, and the isoscalar monopole excitation strength is varied. Fragment yields, directed flow, cluster flow and rapidity slopes change markedly near ε≈0.5.

papers.title: Constraining three-nucleon forces in nuclear lattice effective field theory
papers.short_authors: Serdar Elhatisari, Ulf-G. Meißner, Zhengxue Ren, Shuang Zhang
papers.abstract: Short-range three-nucleon-force terms in nuclear lattice effective field theory are decomposed into locally and non-locally smeared components and supplemented by pair contacts coupled to the density of a third nucleon. Coefficients are constrained using binding energies for nuclei with A=3–40 and neutron-alpha finite-volume energies, yielding a minimal three-nucleon force for future precision studies.

papers.title: Constraints on pion parton distributions at small x from leading-neutron electroproduction data
papers.short_authors: C. Yang, P. C. Barry, W. Melnitchouk, N. Sato
papers.abstract: The authors revisit pion PDFs with a global QCD analysis of pion-nucleus Drell-Yan and leading-neutron electroproduction data, varying data coverage, parameterization and positivity constraints while fitting pion-nucleon splitting functions. The enlarged H1+ZEUS leading-neutron data set reduces parameterization dependence and strongly disfavors a vanishing pion gluon PDF.

papers.title: Do Perturbation Predictors Learn Gene Interactions? Diagnosing Extrapolation in Agentic Screening
papers.abstract: The paper studies unseen gene pairs for which both individual genes appeared during training. It compares neural predictors with an additive baseline and defines additive disagreement as a signal of interaction extrapolation risk. Across eight methods and three Perturb-seq data sets, the specialized predictors do not consistently beat the additive baseline, while larger disagreement tracks larger error.
